glosses: An ongoing winner in a game or contest.

examples.text: The defending champion is expected to defeat his challenger.
Curry, a four-time NBA champion with the Warriors, played for the Wildcats for three seasons between 2006 and 2009, where he was twice named conference player of the year.

glosses: Someone who is chosen to represent a group of people in a contest.

examples.text: Barcelona is eligible to play in FIFA Club World Cup as the champion of Europe.

glosses: Someone who fights for a cause or status.

examples.text: Emmeline Pankhurst was a champion of women's suffrage.
Specific outcomes from this policy included the appointment of a Digital Champion to drive forward the efforts to get more of the excluded to be included.

glosses: Someone who fights on another's behalf.

examples.text: champion of the poor

glosses: A particularly notable member of a plant species, such as one of great size.

examples.text: Pictured above is an actual photograph of a Regal Lily that famed all over the world. It's a champion plant—because in one season it produced a total of 89 blooms from one bulb, an amazing record among lilies.
There was a news clipping there with a photo of a magnificent American elm, which had just been named the champion for its species, the largest of its kind.
He [Matthew Olson] was searching for red maple trees to be tapped for syrup as part of the Stockton Maple Project when he came across the new champion tree.

glosses: Acting as a champion; having defeated all one's competitors.

examples.text: a champion bodybuilder

glosses: Excellent; beyond compare.
Excellent; brilliant; superb; deserving of high praise.

examples.text: "That rollercoaster was champion," laughed Vinny.

glosses: To promote, advocate, or act as a champion for (a cause, etc.).

examples.text: While obviously championing the Bluebell [Railway], Beardmore is keen for the 'big railway' to consider utilising what preserved railways can provide.
